2609.24677.title: TimeLitmus: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Cross-Modal Understanding and Explanation Faithfulness in Event-Conditioned Time-Series Prediction
2609.24677.paper_summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to make predictions from numerical time-series histories and textual events. Yet accuracy alone cannot reveal whether correct answers reflect effective integration of the two inputs or instead arise from event polarity, unimodal priors, or superficial cues. Likewise, plausible explanations may rationalize predictions without faithfully reflecting the evidence that drives model behavior. We introduce TimeLitmus, a diagnostic benchmark for cross-modal understanding and explanation faithfulness in event-conditioned time-series prediction. TimeLitmus contains 4,856 evaluation records across Finance and Traffic, combining natural prediction with controlled counterfactual and contrastive interventions, explanation-targeted faithfulness tests, and systematic shortcut controls. Across ten representative LLMs, standard prediction accuracy substantially overstates reliable cross-modal understanding: Hard Paired Contrast (HPC) pair correctness peaks at only 19.2% in Finance and 11.7% in Traffic, and all ten models show lower-than-expected consistency on Finance series-side controls. Models often recognize scenario relations explicitly yet fail to apply them during independent prediction. Explanation faithfulness shows a similar gap: in Traffic, most models cite the manipulated temporal factor in over 90% of cases, while behavioral support remains below 22%. Human annotators outperform LLMs on matched controlled and hard-pair diagnostics, confirming that these distinctions are recoverable from the inputs. Natural-only adaptation yields selective gains in evidence selection and input sensitivity, but not consistent gains in controlled or hard-pair behavior. The benchmark, evaluation suite, and supervised adaptation data will be released publicly.
2609.24677.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）越來越多地用於從數值時間序列歷史和文本事件中進行預測。<lb/>然而，僅僅依賴準確性並不能揭示正確答案是否反映了兩種輸入的有效整合，或者只是源於事件極性、單模態先驗或表面線索。<lb/>同樣，合理的解釋可能會合理化預測，而不忠實地反映驅動模型行為的證據。<lb/>我們介紹了TimeLitmus，這是一個用於事件條件時間序列預測的跨模態理解和解釋忠實性的診斷基準。<lb/>TimeLitmus包含4,856條評估記錄，涵蓋金融和交通，結合自然預測與控制的反事實和對比干預、針對解釋的忠實性測試以及系統性的捷徑控制。<lb/>在十個代表性的LLMs中，標準預測準確性大大高估了可靠的跨模態理解：在金融中，困難配對對比（HPC）配對的正確率僅達到19.2%，在交通中為11.7%，而所有十個模型在金融系列的控制上顯示出低於預期的一致性。<lb/>模型通常明確識別場景關係，但在獨立預測時卻未能應用這些關係。<lb/>解釋忠實性顯示出類似的差距：在交通中，大多數模型在超過90%的情況下引用了操控的時間因素，而行為支持則低於22%。<lb/>人類標註者在匹配的控制和困難配對診斷中表現優於LLMs，確認這些區別可以從輸入中恢復。<lb/>僅自然適應在證據選擇和輸入敏感性上帶來選擇性增益，但在控制或困難配對行為上並未帶來一致的增益。<lb/>該基準、評估套件和監督適應數據將公開發布。
